reasoning: The extract has two lines on evaluation. The first, "It will be reviewed If applicable, set review date: 08 2021", is a template fragment that gives a review date of August 2021. The second says "We plan to review this policy five years after its implementation and will include a completed Post- Implementation Review template in the final IA." Together these give a plan to evaluate with a timetable (a review five years after implementation) and a vehicle for it (a Post-Implementation Review). The extract carries no citations. It shows no success measures or outcomes to be tracked, no plans to test the policy first, and no reasons why testing would be inappropriate. It does not say what will happen to the review results or whether they will be published. The two dates also sit awkwardly: a 2021 review date next to a five-year review is not reconciled. The strongest counter-example to Level 1 is that a review plan with a timetable looks like Level 2 evaluation. It does not reach Level 2, though, because there are no comprehensive success measures and nothing on testing. A Level 1 reading rests on the review commitment as the only indication of how success will be judged, which is thin. To reach Level 2 the document would need to specify the outcomes to be measured (for example, road safety incidents involving exempt vehicles), explain whether piloting was considered, and describe how the evaluation will be done. For Level 3 it would also need to give reasons for these choices and commit to publishing the results.
